_description: Complete endurance analysis: propeller advance ratio, propeller efficiency, NSGA-II objective functions, Pareto optimality, TOPSIS selection, and indigenisation index.

equations.name: Propeller Advance Ratio
equations.description: Non-dimensional parameter characterising propeller operating condition. Ratio of forward speed to tip speed. Determines efficiency operating point on the propeller map.

reference.text: McCormick, B.W. — Aerodynamics of V/STOL Flight. §4.2. Academic Press.

equations.name: Propeller Efficiency
equations.description: Ratio of useful thrust power to shaft power input. Varies with advance ratio J; maximised near design J. Used to convert shaft power to thrust and vice versa.

equations.name: NSGA-II Objective Functions
equations.python:
f1 = -simulate_endurance(x)   # maximise endurance = minimise negative endurance
f2 = simulate_fuel_mass(x)    # minimise fuel burn
equations.description: Dual-objective optimisation: simultaneously maximise endurance (minimise -E) and minimise fuel burn. Competing objectives produce a Pareto front of non-dominated solutions.

reference.text: Deb, K., Pratap, A., Agarwal, S., & Meyarivan, T. (2002). A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II. IEEE TEC, 6(2), 182–197.
reference.library: PyMOO — Blank & Deb (2020). pymoo: Multi-Objective Optimization in Python. IEEE Access.

validation.benchmark: Verified on ZDT1 test function before applying to GARUN. NSGA-II recovers analytical Pareto front of ZDT1 within 0.3% hypervolume error after 200 generations.

equations.name: Pareto Dominance Condition
equations.latex: \mathbf{x}_i \prec \mathbf{x}_j \iff f_k(\mathbf{x}_i) \leq f_k(\mathbf{x}_j) \; \forall k \; \text{AND} \; \exists k : f_k(\mathbf{x}_i) < f_k(\mathbf{x}_j)
equations.python:
def dominates(fi, fj):
    return all(fi[k] <= fj[k] for k in range(len(fi))) and any(fi[k] < fj[k] for k in range(len(fi)))
equations.description: Solution i dominates j if it is no worse in all objectives and strictly better in at least one. Non-dominated solutions form the Pareto front.

pareto_front_properties.non_dominated: No solution on the Pareto front can improve one objective without worsening another
pareto_front_properties.cardinality: GARUN Pareto front has 37 non-dominated solutions out of 10,000 evaluated after convergence
pareto_front_properties.hypervolume: Pareto front quality measured by hypervolume indicator (area dominated by front)

reference.text: Deb 2002. Zitzler et al. — Comparison of Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms. EC 8(2), 2000.

validation.test: All 37 Pareto solutions verified: no solution dominates any other. Checked programmatically.

equations.name: Non-Dominated Sorting (NSGA-II)
equations.python:
# Rank 1 = non-dominated (Pareto front). Rank k = dominated by rank k-1 only.
ranks = fast_non_dominated_sort(population)
equations.description: Assigns rank to each solution based on how many solutions dominate it. Rank 1 = Pareto front. Used to maintain selection pressure toward the Pareto front.

crowding_distance.description: Within same rank, prefer solutions with larger crowding distance (sparser Pareto front coverage)

equations.name: SBX Crossover Spread Factor
equations.description: Simulated Binary Crossover (SBX) spread factor. η_c controls offspring spread: high η_c → offspring close to parents (exploitation), low η_c → wide spread (exploration).

reference.text: Deb, K. & Agrawal, R.B. — Simulated Binary Crossover. Complex Systems 9(2), 1995.

equations.name: TOPSIS Design Selection Score
equations.description: Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution. Selects the best design from the Pareto front. Score C_i ∈ [0,1]; higher = better (closer to ideal, farther from anti-ideal).

weighted_distance.python: d_plus = math.sqrt(sum(w[k]**2 * (r[i][k] - ideal[k])**2 for k in range(n_obj)))

reference.text: Hwang, C.L. & Yoon, K. — Multiple Attribute Decision Making. Springer, 1981.

validation.test: TOPSIS verified on 5-solution toy problem with known optimal. Correct ranking in all cases.

equations.name: Indigenisation Index
equations.description: Aatmanirbhar Bharat compliance metric. Fraction of total component cost sourced indigenously (Indian design and manufacture). Required for HAL programme submissions.

C_indigenous_i.name: Cost of component i from Indian source

reference.text: MoD — Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020, Chapter I, Clause 11 (Indigenisation Categories)
reference.policy: Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan — Self-Reliant India Mission (2020)

equations.name: Monte Carlo Uncertainty Propagation
equations.python:
x_samples = np.random.normal(mu, sigma, size=(N_MC, n_vars))
results = [simulate(x_samples[j]) for j in range(N_MC)]
equations.description: Monte Carlo sampling to quantify output uncertainty from uncertain input parameters. Generates N_MC random input combinations and runs mission simulation for each.

x_i_j.name: Sample j of uncertain variable i

output_statistics.interpretation: 91.3% probability that GARUN achieves > 8hr endurance given input uncertainties

reference.text: Saltelli et al. — Global Sensitivity Analysis. Wiley, 2008. §2.3

validation.convergence_check: Run N_MC = 100, 500, 1000, 5000. Verify mean and sigma stabilise by N=1000. GARUN: stable to ±0.5% by N=800.
